title: Following two-step instructions
keyIdea: A two-step instruction asks for two things in order, such as "Get your shoes and bring them to the door." To follow it you listen to the end, keep both parts in your head, do the first part first and then the second. If you forget a part, it is fine to ask, "Can you say it again, please?" Saying the steps back helps you remember them.

kid: Gran says, "Get your shoes." That is one job. You get your shoes.
Gran says, "Get your shoes and bring them to the door." That is two jobs!
Listen to the end. Do the first job first. Then do the next job.
Did you forget? That is OK. Ask, "Can you say it again, please?" Then say it back: shoes, then door.
adult: This topic, for ages 3 to 4, is about carrying out an instruction with two parts, such as "Put your cup in the sink and then fetch your coat." It asks a young child to listen to the whole sentence, hold both parts in mind while they act (early working memory), and keep the order. It grows out of being able to pay attention to one thing, and it is the base for following classroom routines later.

In the lab, your child taps one thing Gran asks for, then two things in a first-then order, then gets an object and takes it to a place (shoes to the door, cup to the sink). Next the words hide and they work from memory, with a "Say it again, please" button that is praised, not punished. Last, they put picture cards in order to say the steps back.

Common mistakes: doing only the last part heard (the most recent words are easiest to recall), doing the parts in the wrong order, and doing the first part and then drifting off. Adults often add to the load by giving three or four steps at once, or by talking while the child is busy. Get their attention first, say it once, slowly, and ask them to tell you the two jobs before they start.
Use everyday jobs: "Put your socks in the basket, then come for your story." Point or show as you say each part, and praise your child for asking when they forget.

familyTip: Play "Gran says" at home: give a two-part job such as "Touch the door, then jump" and let your child do it, then swap so they give you a two-part job. Make a mistake on purpose (do it in the wrong order) and let them catch you.

practice.prompt: Gran says, "First clap, then jump." What do you do first?
practice.hint: Listen for the word first. What comes right after it?
practice.explain: Gran said clap first. The word first tells you which job to do now, and then tells you the next job.

practice.prompt: Mum says, "Put your cup in the sink, then get your coat." Ben has {n} toys out, but he does not touch them. What does he do first?
choices: Put his cup in the sink
practice.hint: Which job did Mum say first?
practice.explain: Mum said the cup first, so Ben puts his cup in the sink and then gets his coat. The toys were not part of the job.

practice.prompt: Dad says two jobs. You forget the second one. What do you do?
choices: Ask, "Can you say it again, please?"
practice.hint: Is it OK to ask a grown-up to help you remember?
practice.explain: Asking to hear it again is a good thing to do. Guessing can lead to the wrong job, and doing nothing leaves the job undone.

practice.prompt: Gran says, "Get your shoes and bring them to the door." Mia gets her shoes and sits down with them. She has {n} minutes left before the walk. What did she forget?
choices: To bring them to the door
practice.hint: Gran said two jobs. Mia did one. Which one is left?
practice.explain: Getting the shoes was part one. Bringing them to the door was part two, and Mia has not done it yet.

practice.prompt: Teacher says, "Wash your hands, then sit at the table." How can you say it back?
practice.hint: Say the two jobs in the same order you heard them.
practice.explain: Saying it back in the same order, wash hands then sit down, helps you remember both parts and shows you heard them.

pool.prompt: Gran says, "Touch your nose, then touch your toes." Which is right?
pool.hint: Which part came after the word then?
pool.explain: Nose comes first and toes come second, because Gran said touch your nose, then touch your toes.

pool.prompt: Mum says, "Put the ball in the box and then come for lunch." Tom runs to lunch and leaves the ball. Is that right?
choices: No, the ball goes in the box first
pool.hint: Tom did the last part he heard. What came before it?
pool.explain: Tom only did the last part. Mum asked for the ball in the box first, then lunch.

pool.prompt: How many jobs are in "Get your coat and hang it on the hook"?
pool.hint: Count the things to do: get it, then hang it.
pool.explain: There are two jobs: get your coat, then hang it on the hook.

pool.prompt: Gran says, "Find your hat, then put on your boots." What do you do second?
pool.hint: Second means the job after the first one.
pool.explain: Find your hat is the first job and put on your boots is the second job.

pool.prompt: Dad is talking. You want to remember his two jobs. What helps most?
choices: Listen to the end, then say it back
pool.hint: How can you be sure you have both parts?
pool.explain: Listening to the end and then saying the two jobs back helps you hold both parts in your head.

pool.prompt: Gran says, "Put your {n} blocks in the box, then wash your hands." What do you do first?
choices: Put the blocks in the box
pool.hint: The first job is the one Gran said first.
pool.explain: Putting the blocks away is the first job. Washing your hands comes next, after the blocks.

pool.prompt: Mum says two jobs. Ana does the first one, then stops. There are {n} more minutes till bath time. What should Ana do now?
pool.hint: Mum said two jobs. How many has Ana done?
pool.explain: Ana has done one of the two jobs. She should do the second job now, and ask again if she has forgotten it.

pool.prompt: You did not hear the end of what Gran said. What can you say?
pool.hint: Use kind words to ask Gran for help.
pool.explain: Asking Gran to say it again is the right thing to do, so you can hear both parts before you start.

visual.caption: One job or two jobs? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

items: get your shoes and bring them to the door
wash your hands, then sit down
put your cup in the sink, then get your coat

lab.caption: Flagship lab: do one thing Gran asks, then two things in order, get it and bring it, remember both parts when the words hide, and say the steps back.
